outline.chapter_title: 1. Overview of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational context for the study, introducing the capabilities and limitations of current open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) in handling mathematical tasks. It sets the stage for why specialized models like DeepSeekMath were developed.
subtopics: Introduction to LLMs and their impact on AI research
The specific challenges of structured mathematical reasoning
Comparison between open-source models (e.g., Mistral, CodeLlama) and closed-source leaders (GPT-4, Gemini)
The necessity of domain-specific training data for reasoning tasks
Limitations of current pre-training data sources

outline.chapter_title: 2. DeepSeekMath Corpus: A Data-Centric Approach to Mathematical Pre-Training
outline.description: This chapter details the construction, curation, and validation of the DeepSeekMath Corpus. It explains the methodology behind extracting high-quality mathematical content from public web sources like Common Crawl.
subtopics: Designing a fastText-based classifier for automated data selection
Iterative pipeline for gathering web pages from Common Crawl
Handling data diversity and avoiding bias towards specific domains
Decontamination techniques to prevent benchmark leakage (10-gram filtering)
Selection and evaluation strategies using seed corpora like OpenWebMath
Validation results: Comparing performance across MathPile, Proof-Pile-2, and DeepSeekMath Corpus
Multilingual coverage: The value of English-Chinese bilingual math data

outline.description: This chapter covers the technical process of initializing and training the base model, emphasizing the importance of initialization choice and curriculum learning via corpus distribution.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 vs. General LLMs
'Code Training Helps': Ablation studies on sequential pre-training (Code -> Math) vs. simultaneous training
*The ArXiv Paradox*: Investigating why including arXiv papers did not yield expected improvements in quantitative reasoning
*Turbo-Learning*: The scaling laws observed with 500B tokens of corpus-specific training
*Gradient Descent Landscapes*: Stability and convergence when mixing code tokens with math tokens

outline.chapter_title: 4. From Base to Instruct: Supervised Fine-Tuning and Instruction Patterns
outline.description: This chapter explores how raw base model skills are transformed into an instruction-following agent capable of generating Chain-of-Thought (CoT) solutions.
subtopics: *Instruction Tuning Data Curation*: Construction of GSM8K, MATH, Chinese K-12 datasets in CoT/PoT formats
*Prompt Engineering Styles: Chain-of-Thought vs. Program-of-Thought vs. Tool Integrated Reasoning*
*Evaluation Benchmarks*: Statistical analysis on GSM8K, MATH, SAT, CMATH, MiniF2F*
*Multilingual Reasoning*: Comparative analysis on English vs. Chinese instruction performance
